To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) multicasting can significantly reduce the cost of distributing video content to a large number of users and (ii) the model with multiple titles for download is much more efficient than the single title model.

the performance of the system can be greatly improved by allowing multiple titles to be requested by the user, that the performance can be further improved by reducing the number of times that a title is requested by a user, and that the performance can also be further improved by delaying the delivery of the less frequent titles.

(1) the multicasting of multiple titles on the same link can be optimized by a simple greedy algorithm, and that (2) the multiperiod performance can be improved by a simple heuristic that allows to reduce the number of downloads for each title and to reduce the delivery time of the less frequent titles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficient distribution of a large set of video titles to a large number of users, with the goal of reducing the overall download time and the number of downloads per title.
the design of efficient algorithms for the distribution of multimedia contents in the context of push-VoD.
the design of a novel content distribution system for the managed delivery of multimedia content over DSL networks.
